findings.defect: The headline is billed as a refutation ("the reopening premise is FALSE and now provably so") and carries the route's "strict-progress" verdict, but the lemma constrains run LENGTH not at all: it is a value-propagation identity that every improving run satisfies, including exponentially long ones. It removes a local accounting hope the ROUTE ITSELF invented (no statement in frontier.tex ever asserted it -- rem:impedance says only that the gain of a single switch has no polynomial-range local bound, which lane:impedance-cancels does not contradict), and it rules nothing out. A future round must not read it as an obstruction.
findings.evidence: I re-implemented the first-passage law from the graph and tested lem:rise-bound at every at-rest Max vertex, for every pair t<t', along the LEAST-INDEX run on the paper's own ladder L_n (def:ladder, thm:ladder), whose run length is 2^n-1: L_2..L_6 give run lengths 3,7,15,31,63 with 3,28,180,992,5040 rise-bound checks and ZERO violations (exact Fractions; /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-sig/ladder_rise.py). So a 2^{Omega(N)} improving run in this very paper satisfies the bound. Moreover the proof uses only (i) val_rho is a fixed point of T_rho, (ii) at rest = EVERY action worth at most x(u), (iii) a substochastic row, (iv) p_u<1 by stopping -- all of which hold verbatim at arbitrary out-degree, hence on the published multi-action families where Howard's rule is exponential (Fearnley 2010, Christ-Yannakakis 2023; from memory, unchecked against the sources).

I verified RC/ALH/CL independently (own all-switches loop, exact arithmetic, k=2,3,5,8,13,21): RC L=N-2, ALH L=N-3, CL L=(N-2)/2, all stopping, out-degree two, one switch per round in order k..1.

findings.defect: Presented as a Theorem "strictly sharper than thm:peak-law" and proved with a jump-chain / (I-Q)^{-1}R argument. It is in fact an immediate corollary of the PROOF of thm:peak-law (frontier.tex:3478): observe that for v in Delta not strictly switchable at sigma one has delta(v) = x(sigma-bar(v)) - x(sigma(v)) <= 0, so phi <= P phi off S_sigma and the theorem's own closedness argument applies verbatim -- three lines. The paper now carries exactly that as cor:peak-sharp (frontier.tex:3521), which is STRICTLY STRONGER (peak on A ∩ S_sigma ∩ Delta, not merely on S_t), and whose proof note records that "the weaker form with S_t alone is the round-15 lane route's, and its auditor supplied this one". The route's claim to sharpness holds only against the STATEMENT of thm:peak-law, not against its proof.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex:3478-3546 (thm:peak-law, cor:peak-sharp with its attribution note); git show 9f5a4d7 shows cor:peak-sharp was added by the integration of this very route.

findings.defect: Not new mathematics: the core claim val_sigma|_U = val^{G|_U}_{sigma|_U} is lem:successor-closed (frontier.tex:2091) applied to the frozen game G_sigma. Autonomy makes A := U ∪ {average vertices on the paths} ∪ {sinks} successor-closed in G_sigma (any controlled vertex reachable before another controlled vertex lies in W(u,a) ⊆ U), so lem:successor-closed gives the restriction identity at once. Parts (b) and (c) the route already cites to cor:law-u and cor:ceiling-general/prop:oneplayer-lp. The whole proposition is a repackaging of three existing results, and it closes only the case where the re-used module is self-contained -- near-tautological, since a self-contained module's run IS its own run.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex:2091-2103 (lem:successor-closed), 4056 (cor:law-u), 4037 (cor:ceiling-general), 4264 (prop:oneplayer-lp). The route's own proof reproves the identity via first passage rather than citing lem:successor-closed.

findings.defect: Replacing an r-action state by a rooted binary tree of max nodes is the standard out-degree-two normalisation of the games/MDP literature (it is how def:ssg's binary model is reached from an arbitrary-arity one). It is presented with no attribution by the route, and was integrated with none. Additionally, rem:closed-now-or-never already contained the idea in prose: "A Max vertex whose successor is another Max vertex simulates a three-way choice one round later, and def:damping makes such a tree cheap, so the postponement can be reintroduced with a lag." The genuinely new content is narrower than the lemma's billing: the ceil(log2 r) lag statement and the 15-vertex instance showing the lag is real.

Sharper gap: (i) for NONDEGENERATE one-player stopping games prop:oneplayer-lp forces the improvement orientation to be Holt-Klee, so a superpolynomial one-player family of that kind requires h*_HK(m) to be superpolynomial -- open, and measured only as 1,2,4,6,11 for m<=5, with h*_HK(5)=11 itself unverified; (ii) for DEGENERATE one-player games the Holt-Klee ceiling does not bind (rem:oneplayer-lp) and thm:blowup already supplies h*(m) >= 2^{m/2+1}-2, so there the obstruction is purely REALISATION at N = m^{O(1)} -- and by lane:grid/rem:grid-per-vertex any such family must have a >= 1 and must switch some vertex more than once, which RC, ALH and CL (all one switch per vertex) do not.

verdict:
IS IT NEW? Partly, and the paper has already decided the question: the root agent integrated a trimmed 137-line version at HEAD (commit 9f5a4d7, "frontier.tex: the lane route, trimmed"), so four items are now IN the paper -- lem:rise-bound (3547), cor:peak-sharp (3521, in a form STRONGER than the route's lane:peak-source, supplied by an earlier auditor), lem:max-tree with the Fearnley binarisation gap (3442), and rem:grid-per-vertex carrying lane:grid, RC(k) and the a=0 optimality (5421), plus a paragraph in rem:impedance. Nothing in the route duplicates a pre-existing label outright, but three items are corollary-strength: lane:peak-source falls out of thm:peak-law's PROOF in three lines; lane:autonomy is lem:successor-closed applied to the frozen game plus cor:law-u and cor:ceiling-general; lane:exit-chain is an application of prop:closed-now-or-never whose general limits rem:closed-now-or-never already spells out. Unattributed standard mathematics: the binary-tree binarisation in lane:tree (textbook out-degree-two normalisation) and RC(k) itself (the integration correctly relabels it folklore; the route did not).

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No algorithm is claimed, so no target-equivalent oracle. No polynomial class is claimed. The two "closures" (lane:autonomy, lane:exit-chain) are NOT barriers -- they cover none of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and must be labelled as laws of runs exactly as rem:closed-now-or-never labels its own. The headline lem:rise-bound is not vacuous but it is not an obstruction either: I verified it holds at every at-rest vertex on the ladder L_n under least-index, a run of length 2^n-1 already in this paper, and its proof survives arbitrary out-degree, hence holds on the published families where Howard's rule is exponential. The families RC/ALH/CL are genuine (build(k), proved growth law, verified independently by me at six sizes each in exact arithmetic, stopping, out-degree two, fair coins) -- but all three are LINEAR, so they are cheapenings of a known phenomenon, not lower bounds.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? The proof-level verification is honest and adequate (74232 + 10933 rise-bound instances, both players present, laws recomputed from the graph; families verified from the graph with an independent loop; I reproduced the family results myself). The MEASUREMENT-level verification is not: lane:measured and lane:nminus2 rest on annealing runs that cannot find the route's own trivial families at the same parameters (beat_n7 -> 6 vs RC(7)=7; beat_n9 -> 8 vs RC(9)=9; fixeda a=0 m=7,8 -> 6,6 vs 7,8; fixeda a=1 m=8 -> 5 vs ALH(8)=8; ss_n12/16/20 -> 8,10,9 vs 12,16,20), and the largest-n runs, where the collapse is worst, are omitted from the LaTeX and the JSON. Under the standing rule that is not weak evidence, it is none, and the write-up does not say so.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it: not one architecture but two independent unknowns. (i) Is h*_HK(m) -- the greatest bottom-antipodal height of a HOLT-KLEE AUSO of the m-cube -- superpolynomial? By prop:oneplayer-lp this is exactly the nondegenerate one-player half of the pivot, and it is measured only as 1,2,4,6,11 for m<=5 with the 11 unverified. (ii) For DEGENERATE one-player games the Holt-Klee ceiling does not bind (rem:oneplayer-lp) and thm:blowup already gives h*(m) >= 2^{m/2+1}-2, so there the entire obstruction is REALISATION at N = m^{O(1)}; and by rem:grid-per-vertex any such family must have a >= 1 and must switch some vertex more than once -- which every family this route built (RC, ALH, CL, all exactly one switch per vertex) fails to do. The route's claim that mixture-driven turnarounds are the only architecture its theorems leave open is unsupported; two-player coupling through Min's best response is untouched by both of its closures, as rem:closed-now-or-never already notes.

WOULD INTEGRATING MAKE THE PAPER BETTER OR WORSE? The integration that already happened makes it BETTER and is correctly proportioned; integrating anything further would make it WORSE. Keep (already in): lem:rise-bound, cor:peak-sharp, lem:max-tree with the binarisation gap, rem:grid-per-vertex with RC and the a=0 optimality, and the rem:impedance paragraph. Two small repairs to what is in: lem:max-tree should say the binarisation itself is the standard out-degree-two normalisation and that rem:closed-now-or-never already stated it in prose, and rem:impedance's new paragraph should add one clause saying the bound holds on runs of length 2^n-1 (the ladder) so that it is not later mistaken for an obstruction. Do NOT integrate: lane:peak-source (superseded and weaker than cor:peak-sharp), lane:autonomy/lane:modules (lem:successor-closed + cor:law-u repackaged), lane:exit-chain/lane:budget (an instance of prop:closed-now-or-never, covering none of M1-M6 or def:bsi, with an unproved clause), ALH and CL (both dominated by RC, and the "all three degenerate" claim is false at CL(2)), and above all lane:measured/lane:nminus2 -- the search behind them is calibrated below the trivial construction, and rem:grid-per-vertex already states the same question correctly and better, as Melekopoglou and Condon's. Verdict on the route's own grade: "strict-progress" is too generous. It is honest, competent negative housekeeping that killed a hope it had itself raised, produced one small closed case (a=0, with a folklore witness), and moved the pivot not at all.
